subject.title: PR2/5 durable core: runtime foundation and terminal immutability guard

question: Should the residual durable-runtime invariants extend the existing TaskFlow/task/subagent stores, or should OpenClaw intentionally adopt a second durable_runtime_* lifecycle ledger?
rationale: The PR establishes a broad new persistence, protocol, worker, and ownership boundary that cannot safely be selected by mechanical review while current main already has authoritative durable task and flow owners.

options.title: Extend existing owners
options.body: Refactor the residual invariants into task_runs, flow_runs, subagent state, and their existing APIs so one authoritative lifecycle remains.

options.title: Approve a parallel ledger
options.body: Explicitly sponsor durable_runtime_* as a separate authority and require a written synchronization, migration, rollback, and conflict-resolution contract before merge.

options.title: Pause the implementation stack
options.body: Hold or close implementation PRs until the predecessor RFC has an approved owner boundary and proof plan.

recommendation.title: Extend existing owners
recommendation.body: Refactor the residual invariants into task_runs, flow_runs, subagent state, and their existing APIs so one authoritative lifecycle remains.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation overlaps the TaskFlow, task persistence, subagent mirroring, and restart-recovery surfaces introduced and maintained in this history.
